item.description: Standard deviation of NN intervals in the entire recording.
The square root of the mean of the sum of the squares of differences between adjacent NN intervals.
Number of pairs of adjacent NN intervals differing by more than 50 ms in the entire recording divided by the total number of all NN intervals.
Low values of this index indicate independence between breath and pulse, while high values indicate synchronization reaching maximum when index is equal to 1.

Represents 1% percentile of momental heart rate value. Can be interpreted as lowest heart rate achieved during training session. At hypoxic training positive dynamics revealed when this value is decreasing.

Maximal breath hold time after inhale. This indicator is also a good estimation of fitness condition. For untrained person it is good to be able to hold the breath for 40-50 seconds, and for a trained person it is 60-90 seconds. Illness or fatigue causes the reduction of apnea time to 30-35 seconds. This indicator also refers to Stange test.

Maximal breath hold time after exhale. This indicator is also a good estimation of fitness condition. For untrained person it is good to be able to hold the breath for 30 seconds, and for a trained person it is 60 seconds. This indicator also refers to Hench test.
